correctness.rationale: For each gap length ell, an exhaustive decomposition by surviving endpoint runs gives Q_ell. The disjoint gaps are independent and R=k+sum X_ell. For a>=b+2, the displayed exact polynomial factorization Q_a Q_b-Q_(a-1) Q_(b+1)=(1-z)E has explicitly nonnegative coefficients after division by (1-z); b=0 and b>=1 handled separately, including the sole equality move (2,0). This proves every tail comparison at once. Probability of protected terminals sharing one component is p^S(sum p^(-L_i)-(k-1)), obtained from events where all but at most one gap is complete; strict convexity reverses its balancing order. The binomial upper bound is pointwise, with equality exactly when each gap <=2: a failure-survivor-failure pattern in any longer gap gives positive-probability strict loss. The exact-arithmetic verifier independently reproduced the gap laws, terminal connectivity, polynomial signs, exact extremizers, and finite state enumeration. No finite enumeration is passed off as a proof for unbounded n or arbitrary real p.

originality.rationale: The claim is a joint all-upper-tail optimality and reverse multi-terminal-reliability theorem for a site-percolated cycle with protected terminals. Wagner et al. analyze a distinct two-reserve dynamic Markov colonization/catastrophe survival problem. Frasca et al. optimize expected maximum geometric sensor distance with the opposite set of elements subject to failure; their expected-distance result does not imply the multi-quantile connected-habitat law or reversed protected-terminal connectivity. Hof-Flather and Blowes-Connolly analyze related conservation-placement questions with different models; the latter full text could not be inspected, and no whole-document exclusion is claimed. Additional bibliographic equivalence is possible in rooted reliability/percolation literature; this is a provisional scientific originality pass, not independence certification.
residual_risks: Equivalent result may exist in reliability polynomial, rooted-graph percolation, or stochastic-order literature under a different terminology.
Full text of Blowes–Connolly (2012) could not be reviewed, and only selected pages of Hof–Flather (1996) were visually inspected.

value.rationale: The scientifically motivated reserve-spacing problem has two different natural operational objectives: number of surviving sites in contact with at least one refuge, and continuous functional connectivity among every refuge. The theorem proves the unexpectedly opposing placement rules simultaneously and exactly for every upper-tail threshold; it is not a numerical simulation or routine expectation-only improvement. The sharp n<=3k habitat-coverage cutoff and the non-strict (2,0) exceptional move expose structural boundaries useful in design comparisons. These are rigorous model-level statements without unsupported claims about ecological survival in the field.
